summary:
In 2004, a small rover named Opportunity landed on Mars with a mission expected to last just 90 Martian days. It continued exploring for nearly 15 years, traveling 45.16 kilometers, uncovering evidence of ancient water, and surviving conditions it was never expected to endure. Then, in June 2018, a massive dust storm swept across Mars. Opportunity sent its final signal, and Earth never heard from it again.

MER-B: The Last Signal is an interactive visual novel that tells the story of this extraordinary journey.

Instead of simply presenting the mission through facts and timelines, we invite players to experience it through Opportunity's perspective. Through illustrated scenes, dialogue, narration, and meaningful choices, players witness its discoveries, overcome challenges, and follow its journey from its first sunrise on Mars to its final transmission.

Created for NASA's Discarded Equipment Storytelling Challenge, our project explores how storytelling can preserve the legacy of spacecraft that have completed their missions. The scientific events are real; Opportunity's personality and conversations are fictional interpretations designed to make its story more accessible and emotionally engaging.

We wanted people to remember not only what Opportunity discovered, but what its journey meant.

Because sometimes, the smallest explorers leave the biggest marks.
details:
Project Details — MER-B: The Last Signal

Most people know that NASA has sent rovers to Mars. Far fewer know what happened to those rovers after they landed, what they discovered, or how long they continued working beyond their expected lifetimes. We wanted to tell one of those stories.

MER-B: The Last Signal is a fully playable, story-driven visual novel based on NASA's Opportunity rover. It follows Oppy's journey across nine chapters, with an opening sequence and an epilogue, beginning with its journey to Mars and ending with the loss of communication during the 2018 dust storm.

How the Game Works

The game uses a combination of illustrated environments, character dialogue, narration, voice acting, music, and sound effects to tell Opportunity's story.

Players follow the rover through important moments in its mission, including its landing at Eagle Crater, the discovery of evidence of ancient water, its struggle to escape a Martian sand trap, and the dust storms that threatened its survival.

The game also includes small interactive choices throughout, letting players participate in moments of exploration and decision-making. However, these choices do not change the overall story or its ending. We deliberately kept the historical timeline intact because Opportunity's real journey is the story we want people to experience.

The game is playable on both Windows and web browsers, making it accessible without requiring specialized hardware.

How We Built It

We developed the game using Ren'Py, a visual novel engine, and used GitHub to manage our code and collaborate as a team. Notion helped us organize tasks, develop the script, and coordinate our work.

Because of the limited development time, we used AI-assisted tools for parts of the creative process. ChatGPT helped us generate visual assets, which we further refined using Adobe Photoshop. We also used Chatterbox for character voices.

One of our main challenges was bringing the story, visuals, dialogue, and audio together into a complete experience within the hackathon's short time frame. We encountered some technical difficulties along the way, but resolved them and completed a playable game.

Our Creative Approach

We faced an important question while developing the story: How do you make people care about a machine?

Our answer was to tell the mission from Opportunity's perspective.

In our game, Oppy is curious, hopeful, and sometimes afraid. It talks to Earth, celebrates discoveries, and wonders what lies beyond the next horizon. These conversations and emotions are fictional, but the journey behind them is real.

We made a conscious effort to preserve the actual events, locations, and dates of the mission while using fictional dialogue to connect those events into a personal story. Opportunity's scientific achievements remain central to the experience.

Rather than building a traditional educational game filled with facts and quizzes, we wanted players to learn naturally by following a story. They discover the science behind Opportunity's mission while experiencing the challenges that made those discoveries possible.

Why This Project Matters

Opportunity was designed to operate for just 90 Martian days. Instead, it spent nearly 15 years exploring another planet, helping scientists understand Mars's geological history and its ancient water environments.

Behind that achievement were years of engineering, scientific research, problem-solving, and dedication from people on Earth.

Yet as technology advances and new missions begin, older spacecraft can gradually disappear from public attention. Their work remains important, even when their missions are over.

That is what we wanted to address through NASA's Discarded Equipment Storytelling Challenge.

Our goal is not just to teach players what Opportunity discovered, but to help them understand why its journey deserves to be remembered. We hope that someone who has never heard of MER-B can finish our game knowing its story, appreciating the people who made the mission possible, and perhaps becoming a little more curious about space exploration.

Opportunity was a machine. It never actually felt fear, happiness, or loneliness. But its journey represented something deeply human: our curiosity to explore places we may never reach ourselves.

And even though its final signal was received years ago, we believe its story still deserves to be told.
